clarification.reason: Development errors confuse the underlying product with incidental reporting or transfer language, and miss explicit gift/prepaid-card and vehicle/personal-loan contexts. Clarify that single classification decision without adding examples, identifiers, code, or changing the system prompt.
clarification.instruction: Classify the evidence into exactly one known bucket: `Checking or savings account`, `Credit card`, `Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports`, `Debt collection`, `Money transfer, virtual currency, or money service`, `Mortgage`, `Payday loan, title loan, personal loan, or advance loan`, `Prepaid card`, `Student loan`, `Vehicle loan or lease`. Identify the financial product and provider whose conduct is disputed, not merely a legal citation or an incidental payment method. A complaint about an identified mortgage, education loan, vehicle financing, credit card, or personal/payday/installment loan keeps that product category even when it mentions credit reporting or collection. Use Debt collection when the central conduct is a debt collector's demand, debt validation, collection lawsuit, or garnishment; use Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports when the central target is a credit bureau, report, inquiry, or reporting service rather than an identified lender's product. Gift cards, stored-value cards, payroll cards, and benefit-disbursement cards belong to Prepaid card, including disputes about funds or transfers from those cards. Distinguish a bank deposit account's servicing, debit-card purchases, or charge disputes from a remittance, payment-processing, digital-wallet, or virtual-currency service. Use the whole narrative to resolve ambiguity and select the most supported category; do not infer a credit card solely from a purchase dispute or a bank account solely from the word account.
